title: Emit reason codes + tracing for workload-aware batching profile selection
author: Julian Moore
body: Summary: This PR adds explicit reason codes for workload-aware batching profile selection and wires them into structured metrics + tracing so we can answer “what profile did we pick and why?” during canary + rollout. Motivation: As we introduce SLO-tier defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient) we need explainability for operators and for our own regression triage. Today, selection is implicit in scheduler logs and hard to aggregate. This change emits a small, bounded set of reason codes and attaches them to a low-cardinality metric and to a trace span so that we can (a) break down latency/cost by effective profile and (b) understand which policy/constraint caused the selection without parsing logs. Scope: runtime scheduler decision instrumentation only (no policy logic changes, no knob changes). Reason codes are emitted at the final “effective profile” boundary after overrides + constraints have been resolved. Reason codes (v1): TIER_DEFAULT (selected tier default for model family/hw class); ROUTE_OVERRIDE (route policy explicitly selected a tier/profile); TENANT_OVERRIDE (Dedicated/tenant-level override forced); MODEL_CONSTRAINT_FALLBACK (requested tier incompatible; fell back to nearest compatible profile); OVERLOAD_MODE (overload backpressure path forced conservative/alternate profile); SAFETY_GUARDRAIL (guardrail forced smaller batch / lower wait budget). Telemetry: 1) Counter: redwood.runtime.batching.profile_selection_total{tier,reason_code,model_family,hw_class,is_streaming} incremented once per request at admission, using model_family (not full model name) and hw_class (e.g., h100/a100/l4) to keep cardinality bounded. 2) Gauge/hist (existing) labels: plumb “effective_tier” into existing queue/latency attribution context (no new high-card tags). 3) Structured event (debug-only): scheduler emits a structured log payload with selected profile + reason_code + minimal inputs (prompt_len_bucket, concurrency_bucket) behind a runtime flag for targeted investigations. Tracing: Adds a span batching.profile_select under the request root span with attributes: effective_tier, reason_code, model_family, is_streaming, prompt_len_bucket. The span is created only when tracing is enabled and respects existing sampling; no new sampling policy introduced. API/compat: No public API changes. These signals are internal telemetry. Follow-ups: Metric tier labels/cardinality controls are being tightened in PR-28492; this PR intentionally avoids route_id / tenant_id labels. Dedicated override precedence is handled in PR-28503 (this PR just reports TENANT_OVERRIDE when that path is active). Testing: Added unit tests for reason code mapping across (a) pure tier default, (b) route override, (c) incompatibility fallback, (d) overload mode. Added a light integration test that asserts span attributes are present when tracing enabled. Rollout: Safe to land behind existing telemetry pipelines; the counter is additive and uses standard naming conventions. SRE note: initial dashboard panels can key off reason_code to validate expected selection distribution during canary (e.g., low MODEL_CONSTRAINT_FALLBACK unless we’re missing profiles).
commits: runtime/scheduler: add ProfileSelectionReason enum + mapping helper
runtime/telemetry: emit profile_selection_total counter with bounded labels
tests: cover reason code mapping + overload-mode path
docs(internal): update telemetry README for batching selection signals
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Please confirm we’re not introducing unbounded cardinality. Specifically: do not add model name / route id / tenant id labels. Also, can we guarantee reason_code is a fixed set (not stringly-typed)?

Julian Moore (author): Confirmed. Labels are model_family + hw_class + is_streaming + tier + reason_code. reason_code is a closed enum compiled into the runtime; metric exporter maps it to a stable small string set. No model name / route / tenant dimensions added.
Logan Wright: For the counter name, prefer *_total suffix and keep tag keys aligned with our taxonomy. Also, do we need structured logs if we already have traces?

Julian Moore (author): Updated to redwood.runtime.batching.profile_selection_total and tag keys match runtime taxonomy (tier, reason_code, model_family, hw_class, is_streaming). Structured log is behind a flag and meant for cases where tracing is disabled in Dedicated environments; can remove if we think it’s redundant.

Sofia Ivanova: Overload mode reason should be mutually exclusive with others, right? Make sure we don’t emit OVERLOAD_MODE when it was a normal tier default with some queue pressure but not actually overload mode.

Julian Moore (author): Good catch. I changed the selection boundary to only set OVERLOAD_MODE when overload_mode_state == ACTIVE (the same predicate used for load shed/backpressure). Normal “high queue depth” without overload stays on the underlying default/override reason.
Caleb Johnson: Span attribute set looks fine, but please ensure prompt_len_bucket is a small set and not raw lengths. Also ensure we don’t create the span when tracing disabled to avoid overhead.
Julian Moore (author): prompt_len_bucket is the existing 6-bucket enum used by scheduling heuristics (P0..P5). Span creation is under if (tracer->enabled()).
Rafael Mendes: For on-call, I’d like a quick way to search logs for fallback/overload selection. Is there an error-level log? Also any perf risk?

Julian Moore (author): No error-level log. The counter + trace span should be enough for dashboards/triage. Perf overhead is minimal: one counter increment + enum mapping; span only on sampled traces. Unit tests added for mapping path.
Allison Grant: Approved with the condition that we add a comment in code about cardinality constraints and explicitly forbid adding route/tenant/model labels without review.
Julian Moore (author): Added a comment in batching_metrics.cc and a short note in docs/internal/telemetry/batching_selection.md.
release_notes: Internal telemetry: added profile selection reason codes and batching.profile_select trace span to support workload-aware batching SLO-tier rollout.
